citation.title: COP29 is for oil deals
citation.type: NGO investigation (web page); no author or publication date in the extracted text; year inferred from meeting dates of 3 and 13 September 2024 and 'this month' COP29

question: Whether Azerbaijan, as COP29 host, used its position to facilitate discussion of new oil and gas deals, shown through an undercover approach by a fictitious oil and gas investor (EC Capital) offering COP29 sponsorship.
data: Two undercover meetings: with the COP29 partnerships team (3 September 2024) and with COP29 CEO Elnur Soltanov (13 September 2024), plus follow-up contract negotiation and an introduction to a SOCAR vice president. Background figures cited from earlier Global Witness and other work. No delegate or participant list data is used.
method: Undercover investigation: a Global Witness investigator posed as an oil and gas investor, recorded what COP29 officials offered in return for a $600,000 sponsorship. Narrative case study, not a count of delegates. Background claims link to other sources (e.g. Corporate Europe Observatory on lobbyist attendance; earlier Global Witness COP27 and COP28 lobbyist counts), whose methods are not described here.

definitions.term: fossil fuel lobbyist / oil and gas lobbyists
definitions.definition: Not defined. Used loosely for industry representatives at COP; the fictitious investor is said to stand for them figuratively.
definitions.quote: figuratively it represents the army of oil and gas lobbyists who have, in recent years, descended on these climate talks.

definitions.definition: Applied to one person holding two roles (COP29 CEO and deputy energy minister) and facilitating oil and gas investment talks; also applied to COP28 president being CEO of the national oil company. Not formally defined.
definitions.quote: In an apparent conflict of interest, acknowledging his two hats as COP29 CEO and Azerbaijan’s deputy energy minister

definitions.definition: Illustrated by the COP28 president also leading the national oil company; not defined.
definitions.quote: The conflict of interest was laid bare by Al Jaber himself.

definitions.term: undue influence / private gain (UN code of ethics for COP officials)
definitions.definition: Cites the code of ethics for COP officials as forbidding use of the role for private gain. The UNFCCC replied that the investigation falls under a different document, the Code of Conduct for UNFCCC Events.
definitions.quote: forbids the use of their roles “to seek private gain”

definitions.term: Code of Conduct for UNFCCC Events
definitions.definition: Described only as distinct guidance from the Code of Ethics for COP officials; content not described.
definitions.quote: this investigation does not refer to activities covered by the Code of Conduct for UNFCCC Events

definitions.definition: Not defined. States that governments choose who represents them as delegates.
definitions.quote: Governments decide which countries host COP, and who represents them as delegates.

definitions.definition: No definition. SOCAR and ADNOC are treated as state oil companies tied to the host state; SOCAR and the COP29 team are called directly linked to the state.
definitions.quote: both directly linked to the Azerbaijan state

definitions.definition: Sponsorship packages are said to bring COP badges; badge types (Party, overflow, observer) are not mentioned.
definitions.quote: They pitch a $600,000 package, which gets EC Capital five COP badges

proxies.indicator: Companies whose profits depend on extraction of oil, gas and coal, and a coal-power operator named as an example (SSE, 11 fossil-fuel power stations); a refinery builder (Hassan Allam). No explicit rule for classification.
proxies.quote: companies whose profits depend on the extraction of oil, gas and coal have bankrolled the annual talks

proxies.indicator: A count of 2,400 industry representatives; how they were identified is not stated here (links to a separate Global Witness press release).
proxies.quote: A record 2,400 industry representatives showed up, and they were hard at work.
proxies.page: What on Earth are they doing?

proxies.indicator: UNFCCC rule that lobbyists name the company they work for when registering.
proxies.quote: In June 2023, organisers announced that lobbyists would have to identify the company they work for when registering for future summits.

proxies.indicator: Delegate count of an industry group at COP1.
proxies.quote: The Global Climate Coalition, an industry group that lobbied against climate science, sent 25 delegates

findings.claim: COP29 organisers agreed in writing to facilitate oil deal discussions with SOCAR in return for a $600,000 sponsorship.
findings.quote: They have, in writing, promised to facilitate discussions about an oil deal at a UN climate summit, in return for cash.

findings.claim: Sponsorship packages carry COP badges, so sponsorship is one route by which oil and gas firms obtain access.
findings.quote: They pitch a $600,000 package, which gets EC Capital five COP badges

findings.claim: COP29 openly invited the oil industry to take part.
findings.quote: COP29 is explicit that it wants every sector to participate, meaning the oil industry is invited.

findings.claim: Previous COPs have been heavily attended by oil and gas representatives (asserted, with a link to a Corporate Europe Observatory investigation).
findings.quote: previous COPs have almost all been awash with representatives of the oil and gas industry.

findings.claim: At COP28 the president was the chief executive of the national oil company ADNOC.
findings.quote: when it appointed Sultan Al Jaber, the CEO of their national oil company ADNOC, to chair the talks.

findings.claim: Sponsor eligibility rules (Race to Zero or a national pledge) were weak and could be removed from the contract.
findings.quote: COP sponsors must be a member of the UNFCCC’s Race to Zero program

findings.claim: Authors conclude that UNFCCC safeguards were bypassed.
findings.quote: whatever guardrails the UNFCCC put up have been bypassed by lobbyists and fossil fuel powers.

limitations.point: Contains no count of delegates, no list-of-participants analysis, no breakdown by country, sector or badge type. It cannot answer Q1 or Q2 directly.
The 2,400 COP28 industry figure and the 'awash' claim are asserted without method here; the method sits in linked pages not read.
Single case built around one fictitious firm; the authors say it is not a real entity and cannot sign deals.
limitations.quote: As a bogus entity, EC Capital can’t sign oil and gas deals or sponsorship contracts.

limitations.point: Reply of the other side: COP29 team and SOCAR did not respond; the UNFCCC declined comment but said the code Global Witness cited does not apply; Azerbaijani media said facilitating discussions is not a conflict of interest.
limitations.quote: facilitating discussions about fossil fuel investments at COP29 is not a conflict of interest.

limitations.point: Advocacy publication with a stated position (calls for scrapping corporate sponsorship); no author named or publication date in the extracted text; not peer reviewed.
limitations.quote: Scrapping corporate sponsorship is within the UNFCCC’s power

limitations.point: No instructions addressed to a reader or AI were found in the text.
